prompt: aiohttp FormData add_field bytes value no filename fallback
answer:
In aiohttp 3.x, passing a `bytes`, `bytearray`, or `memoryview` value without a filename falls back to using the field name as the filename:

```python
form.add_field("data", b"content")
# filename becomes "data"
```

If `content_transfer_encoding` is also `None`, aiohttp emits a `DeprecationWarning` recommending that you explicitly provide `filename` or use `io.BytesIO` instead. [aiohttp.formdata](https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/v3.12.14/_modules/aiohttp/formdata.html#FormData)

In aiohttp v4, passing bytes no longer creates a file field unless `filename` is explicitly provided. [CHANGES/8303.breaking.rst](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/7275bea9eae591d5246b8fd9e2e9ba004b6f30f7/CHANGES/8303.breaking.rst)
